description: Questions over the Pagila fixture. Gold SQL is the source of truth; `expected` rows are a snapshot of it (python -m dev_tools.evals snapshot). Rentals only span 2022-05-24..28 while payments span 2022-01..07, so a payment can precede its rental.

cases.question: What are the top 5 films by revenue?

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT f.title, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.title ORDER BY revenue DESC, f.title LIMIT 5

cases.question: How many customers does each store have?

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) FROM customer GROUP BY store_id ORDER BY store_id

cases.question: Which film category has the most films, and how many?

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: Which film or films were rented the most times, and how many times?
cases.description: Two films tie at 4 rentals. A 'top 3' phrasing would be ambiguous because four films tie at 3.

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT f.title, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.title HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM rental r2 JOIN inventory i2 ON i2.inventory_id = r2.inventory_id GROUP BY i2.film_id) t) ORDER BY f.title

cases.question: What is the revenue of each store, based on the store that holds the rented inventory?

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id GROUP BY i.store_id ORDER BY i.store_id

cases.question: Which 3 countries have the most customers, and how many each?

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT co.country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY n DESC, co.country LIMIT 3

cases.question: Who is the customer who spent the most, and how much?

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT cu.first_name || ' ' || cu.last_name AS customer, SUM(p.amount) AS total FROM payment p JOIN customer cu ON cu.customer_id = p.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_id, cu.first_name, cu.last_name ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What is the average film length?
Which film category generates the most revenue?
cases.description: A view (sales_by_film_category) answers this without the payment joins; correct, but it hides whether the payment foreign-key chain works.

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON fc.film_id = i.film_id JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What is the top film category by revenue in store 2?
cases.description: Hard: no view covers it, so it needs the payment foreign-key chain. 'Store 2' is ambiguous: the store that holds the inventory (Drama) or the store the paying customer belongs to (Documentary). Both are accepted; a future clarification card should ask which is meant.

gold.label: inventory_store
gold.sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON fc.film_id = i.film_id JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id WHERE i.store_id = 2 GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1

gold.label: customer_store
gold.sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payment p JOIN customer cu ON cu.customer_id = p.customer_id JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON fc.film_id = i.film_id JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id WHERE cu.store_id = 2 GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: For customers of store 1, what are the top 3 countries by revenue?

gold.label: primary
gold.sql: SELECT co.country, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payment p JOIN customer cu ON cu.customer_id = p.customer_id JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id WHERE cu.store_id = 1 GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 3
